LIMITATION OF THE GAP METRIC — revised 2 Oct after reading the retail basis notes.

CORRECTION to the earlier version of this note: mix does NOT contaminate the gap the way I first wrote. Caterpillar reports CI retail sales in "price neutral dollars and based on unit sales as reported by dealers" (Ex 99.2, 2Q 2026). Both sides of the gap are therefore price-neutral dollar measures of units, so a shift toward larger machines raises BOTH and largely cancels.

What does NOT cancel: (1) reported CI sales include parts and services, which have no counterpart in a retail series that measures machines to end users; (2) the disclosed dealer-inventory dollars are current-price, while the gap is price-neutral; (3) currency translation may be treated differently on the two sides; (4) the retail percentage is applied to a reported-sales base, because Caterpillar publishes retail only as a percentage.

Net effect: the gap is a directional and relative measure of dealer stocking, NOT a dollar measurement. Where a disclosed dealer-inventory dollar exists, show it alongside the gap — do not let the gap stand in for it.
VALIDATION TEST — does the gap actually measure dealer stocking?

CONCEPTUAL RELATION, NOT AN ACCOUNTING IDENTITY: shipments to dealers are roughly retail sales to end users plus the change in dealer inventory. Because the two disclosures differ in price basis, scope, parts and services, and possibly currency (rows 33-36), row 40 is a DIRECTIONAL dollar estimate of the year-over-year change in the build, build(t) less build(t-4). Rows 41-42 are what Caterpillar actually disclosed. Only the SIGN can be tested against them.

CI MARGIN, REPORTED vs EX-TARIFF (Q4 2025 - Q2 2026 only)

Adds back the disclosed unfavorable manufacturing costs, which Caterpillar said largely reflected tariffs. DERIVED. Q2 2026 has no CI manufacturing-cost figure; column I instead uses the 340 bps tariff impact disclosed on the Q2 2026 call. DIFFERENT METHOD: column I is not comparable with G-H.
Tariff-related cost $mm: G-H disclosed mfg costs (largely tariffs, SOURCED); I = 340 bps x sales (DERIVED)
Tariff drag (bps): G-H workbook method; I = 340 bps disclosed on the call

G-H are the disclosed unfavorable CI manufacturing-cost figures (SOURCED). Caterpillar said they 'largely reflected' higher tariff costs, so treating them as the full tariff effect is an approximation. I is the 340 bps disclosed on the Q2 2026 call (CFO Kyle Epley, SOURCED), converted to about $284M here (DERIVED). G-H and I use different methods; do not read them as a trend.

READ (INTERPRETIVE): Q4 2025 reported 14.9% is the series low; ex-tariff it sits near 20.9%, inside the 19.6-20.4% band of the surrounding quarters. Our reading is that the trough was mainly a tariff cost shock rather than demand or execution; manufacturing costs are not purely tariffs, and the Q4 2025 profit bridge leaves a $14M unitemized residual. It is NOT one-time: tariffs recur while in force. CI was still carrying about 509 bps (workbook method) in Q1 2026 and 340 bps (disclosed) in Q2 2026. For Q3 2026, management expects tariff costs of around $600 million with about 50% incurred in Construction Industries (CFO Kyle Epley, Q2 2026 call).

EX-TARIFF SEQUENCE: about 20.9% -> 26.5% -> 26.7%. Reported moves 14.9% -> 21.4% -> 23.3% (SOURCED), about 840 bps (DERIVED; +/-10 bps from one-decimal rounding). Lower tariff pressure and volume leverage with price realization both contributed (INTERPRETIVE), but the disclosures do not support a consistent split.

CAVEAT — do not read ex-tariff margin as underlying performance. Price realization swung from -$60M to +$356M to +$309M largely to RECOVER tariffs. Removing the tariff cost while keeping the price taken to offset it double-counts the benefit. Ex-tariff margin is therefore an UPPER BOUND on underlying improvement. The cleanest genuine component is volume leverage.

IEEPA RECOVERIES: Q2 2026 operating profit included $392M of expected IEEPA tariff recoveries (SOURCED). CFO Kyle Epley stated "the majority of this amount reflected in corporate items" (SOURCED). The CI share was not disclosed, so CI segment margin (23.3%) is unlikely to be materially affected; that is an INFERENCE, not a confirmed exclusion. The recovery IS one-time; the tariff costs are not. Management expects full-year 2026 tariff costs of around $2.2 billion, excluding approximately $400 million of expected IEEPA tariff recoveries, at the low end of its prior range (CFO Kyle Epley, Q2 2026 call).

HEADLINE: Q4 2025 CI reported margin 14.9%, tariff-related drag ~604 bps (workbook method). Q1 2026 ~509 bps (workbook method). Q2 2026 340 bps (disclosed on the call). Ex-tariff: ~20.9% / ~26.5% / ~26.7% (upper bound, see row 62).

BOTH contributed, and the split cannot be measured on a consistent basis. Normalization from a tariff-depressed base is part of the recovery; volume leverage plus price realization is the rest, real but partly price taken to recover an external cost, so it should be described as "price recovering tariffs plus volume leverage", never as efficiency or cost control.
